findings.finding: The +24.41% 20-day run-up is two sessions and no company news: 146.0p (26 Aug) -> 162.5p (27 Aug, 1,059,995 shares) -> 195.0p (28 Aug, 678,941 shares) against a ~20k/day norm, and the Investegate day archive shows NO Kooth RNS on either 27 or 28 August 2026. The cause was a Canaccord Genuity flash note on the $18bn Meta settlement (announced 26 Aug). The print is the first management communication since, and management cannot contract-confirm it: California's share is $1.5-2.1bn spread over ten years, earmarked only for 'prevention or remediation of mental health or other harms to young Californians', still awaiting a judge's approval, with not a dollar allocated to any vendor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Kooth reprices violently on US-state funding news and the moves do not persist: -16% in a day on the Pennsylvania termination notice (18 Oct 2024) and +16.79% on the 2025 Full Year Results (15 Apr 2026), against a median absolute results-day move of 2.61% over the twelve observed RNS prints in the baseline. The nearest analogue for an un-validated gap is the present one: the stock has already surrendered 5.9% of the 195p peak and the 5-day run-up is -0.81%, so the fade has begun without the company having said anything.
findings.original_quote: Canaccord Genuity has published a flash note on Kooth (LON: KOO) suggesting that the $18bn Meta settlement has highlighted the mental health of youths and US state clients of Kooth mental health services are due to receive significant amounts of cash. The California attorney general claims that the money is earmarked for mental health and Kooth could receive additional work. The share price rebounded 32.2% to 195p. [UK Investor Magazine, 2026-08-30]
findings.why_not_priced: The move itself is obviously priced - that is the point. What is not priced is the QUALITY of it, which the run-up number cannot see. If an institution had taken the other side of 1.74m shares (4.8% of the 36,694,683 in issue) a TR-1 would have followed within the DTR5 window; none has, to 22 September. The only Holding(s) in Company RNS since (16 Sept, 13:23) is a technical transfer of the existing River UK Micro Cap holding to Liontrust at 6.0659% on an FCA change-of-control approval, not a purchase. So the marginal buyer of the gap is undisclosed and sub-3% - retail and momentum, not a re-rating by a holder who will sit through a disappointing statement. If the market had priced a durable re-rating the stock would have held 195p rather than drifting to 183.5p on falling volume, and at least one 3% notification would exist.
findings.independence: The cause is corroborated by a second, independent domestic outlet on a different date: Share Talk's weekly small-cap movers, 31 Aug 2026 - 'Kooth (AIM: KOO) rebounded 32.2% to 195p after Canaccord Genuity highlighted potential opportunities arising from the $18 billion Meta settlement' - https://www.share-talk.com/share-talk-weekly-small-cap-movers-shakers-monday-31st-august-2026/. The settlement's terms are independently sourced to the California Attorney General's own release, https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-secures-transformative-17-billion-settlement-meta (2026-08-26).

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue bar requires an H2 that reverses the trend of the last five halves. Kooth's own compiled consensus (10 Apr 2026) is FY26 revenue GBP63.1m; H1 2026 came in at GBP30.8m, so H2 must deliver GBP32.3m against an H2 2025 of GBP31.2m (FY25 GBP63.3m less H1 25 GBP32.088m) - +3.5% year on year - while California product development revenue continues 'planned tapering' and sterling is running ~1% stronger against the dollar in H2 2026 (~1.342) than in H2 2025 (~1.33). H1 2026 revenue itself FELL 4.0% year on year. The 29 July trading update reaffirmed only the HALF ('Performance for the half year ended 30 June 2026 is in line with expectations') and made no FY26 statement at all; 23 September is the first FY26 outlook statement since 8 April.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is precisely the line that sold the 2025 print. At the 23 Sept 2025 H1 results - also preceded by a July trading update - Kooth's outlook section quantified an FX haircut for the first time ('the expected impact would be to reduce full year consensus median revenue of GBP66.8m by c.2-3% and consensus median adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.2m by c.6-8%') and the stock fell 5.00% on the day, the baseline's second-largest negative reaction. The 29 July 2026 half-year trading update, which likewise declined to address the full year, fell 3.50%.
findings.original_quote: FY2026 Revenue (Median) GBP63.1m; Adjusted EBITDA (Median) GBP10.4m; EPS, diluted (Median) 6.8p. The information on this page was consolidated on 10 April 2026. [Kooth plc Investor Hub, Analyst Consensus]
findings.why_not_priced: Net of the rest of the company, this is a genuine two-sided call and that is why I size it small: H2 2026 gets the first full half of the State of Michigan contract ($2.6m annualised, signed only in January 2026 after the delays Kooth blamed for FY25), the DWP-funded employment-and-mental-health programmes launching across the West Midlands, South Yorkshire and Cambridgeshire, 14 new UK contracts, and the UK Soluna launch into the autumn school term. Those could carry GBP32.3m. What is unpriced is that with FOUR analysts covering a name doing $228k/day, nobody has published a refreshed FY26 model since April - the consensus page the market is anchored to is 5.5 months old and predates both the July update and the Meta-note re-rating. If the market had worked the arithmetic the stock would not be 63% below its own consensus 303-330p target with zero published preview.
findings.independence: The H1 2025 comparative that fixes H2 2025 at GBP31.2m is from a different document - the audited-basis H1 2025 results PDF, https://investors.kooth.com/docs/koothplclibraries/archive/results/half-year-results-2025.pdf (total revenue 32,088). Shares the 29 July 2026 trading update RNS with nothing else in this list, since I dropped the reported-quarter finding that also rested on it.

findings.finding: Adjusted EBITDA is where Kooth has systematically sandbagged, and the FY26 bar looks low. At the 23 Sept 2025 H1 results Kooth guided FY25 consensus adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.2m down by 'c.6-8%' for FX - an implied GBP9.4-9.6m - and then delivered GBP11.3m, described in its own FY25 RNS as 'ahead of expectations': an ~18% beat against its own guided number. FY26 consensus adjusted EBITDA is GBP10.4m; H1 2026 alone is GBP5.0-5.4m against H1 2025's GBP1.6m, so H2 has only to match H1 to clear it, and the H1 2025 margin drag (gross margin -19.6ppt on front-loaded California user marketing, 'intentionally weighted towards H1 2025') is not repeating. Net cash also ROSE in the half, GBP21.6m at Dec 2025 to GBP23.1m at Jun 2026, so the -GBP6.58m cash generation that accompanied the 2025 print is absent.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When Kooth has confirmed or beaten on adjusted EBITDA the market has paid: +11.74% on the 28 Jan 2026 Trading Update and +4.67% on the 8 Apr 2026 Full Year Results, the two most recent scheduled releases in the baseline where the EBITDA line was the good news. The offsetting precedent is that an EBITDA beat has never been enough on its own when the outlook section carried a haircut (23 Sept 2025, -5.00%), which is why this is sized below the two negatives combined rather than above them.
findings.original_quote: The Group expects to deliver revenue and adjusted EBITDA in line with expectations for the year before accounting for the potential impact of foreign exchange movements. At current rates the expected impact would be to reduce full year consensus median revenue of GBP66.8m by c.2-3% and consensus median adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.2m by c.6-8%. [Kooth plc, Unaudited Half Year Results, 23 September 2025, 'Financial outlook']
findings.why_not_priced: The valuation says nobody has done this sum. At 183.5p on 36,694,683 shares the market capitalisation is ~GBP67m and, less GBP23.1m of net cash, the enterprise value is ~GBP44m - 4.2x the FY26 consensus adjusted EBITDA of GBP10.4m, for a business whose H1 adjusted EBITDA tripled. If the market had priced an EBITDA beat the stock would be trading on the run-up it got from a Meta read-through rather than despite a 4.2x EV/EBITDA, and at least one of the four brokers would have published a raised number since 10 April; none has. The honest counterweight, and the reason this is +1.3 and not +3: FY26 consensus diluted EPS of 6.8p puts the same stock on 27x earnings, so the gap between adjusted EBITDA and statutory profit is large (capitalised development amortisation), and the results statement is exactly where that gap becomes visible line by line.
findings.independence: The FY25 outcome is from a separate RNS on a separate date: '2025 revenue was GBP63.3m (2024: GBP66.7m)... Adjusted EBITDA was ahead of expectations at GBP11.3m in 2025 (2024: GBP15.8m)' - https://investors.kooth.com/rns-alerts/archive/2026/080426.asp (2026-04-08). The FY26 consensus level is from the company's analyst-consensus page, which this finding shares with the revenue finding above; the two use the same page for OPPOSITE lines (revenue vs EBITDA) and are otherwise independent.

outside_window.finding: The California cliff is the dominant value driver and it resolves far outside this window. California's CYBHI Behavioral Health Virtual Services Platform funding - Soluna plus Brightline's BrightLife Kids, a $680m state commitment of which Kooth's share has been reported at $271m over four years - runs to 30 June 2027, and Kooth has 'now entered the fourth year of the contract'. FY2027 consensus revenue of GBP60.8m (only -3.6% on FY26) implicitly assumes continuity or replacement. Any re-procurement decision, and any actual allocation of California's $1.5-2.1bn Meta settlement share to a youth mental-health platform, lands in 2027 and later - not on 23 September. Management may reference it; it cannot be resolved in one session.

The Meta settlement itself was still awaiting judicial approval when it was announced on 26 August 2026, and California's payment is structured over ten years. Court approval and any state-level appropriation of those funds are the events that would validate the 27-28 August re-rating, and both sit well past 23 September 2026.

baseline_tension: My evidence AGREES with the lean and with the run-up, which is the weakest place this stage can land: priced_lean_pct is -1.221 and lean_components shows it is 100% the runup term because anchor_covered is false, so on this name the lean and the free control (-run_up_20d_pct) are one number wearing two hats and a negative call is nearly indistinguishable from shorting the run-up with no research. What the research adds that the control cannot see is (a) the run-up has no company-announced cause at all - verified against the Investegate day archive for 27 and 28 August - and no disclosed institutional buyer took the other side of 1.74m shares, so it is a weak-handed gap rather than a re-rating; (b) the FY26 revenue arithmetic, which is independent of the tape; and (c) a genuine POSITIVE, the EBITDA sandbagging pattern, which cuts against the lean and is why I emit -2.0 rather than anything larger. Stripped of the run-up-dependent finding my research nets to -1.2 + 1.3 = +0.1, and that is the honest measure of what this hunt adds over the free control.

lessons_applied: DROPPED the reported-quarter finding entirely (-0.8), on two rules at once. 'A finding whose own text argues against it': its supporting analogue was the 23 Sept 2025 print, where the new disclosure was a statutory loss of GBP1.255m and cash generation of -GBP6.580m behind GBP1.6m of adjusted EBITDA - and none of that repeats in 2026, where net cash ROSE from GBP21.6m to GBP23.1m in the half and EBITDA tripled. And 'two findings resting on one document are one finding': it shared the 29 July trading update with the FY26 revenue finding. Its surviving substance is in conviction_note and in the EBITDA finding's counterweight.

The revenue finding -1.0 -> -1.2 with a band of [-4.0, +1.0]; the EBITDA finding +1.0 -> +1.3 with [-0.5, +4.0]; the run-up finding -1.2 -> -1.5 with [-5.0, +0.5]. The findings now sum to -1.4 and I emit -2.0, slightly larger, which is only defensible because the name's distribution is wide; it is NOT larger still, because 'positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with' and my dominant negative agrees with a lean that is 100% the free control.
